summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with a history of ESRD on hemodialysis, diabetes, peripheral vascular disease with bilateral below-knee amputations, and paroxysmal atrial flutter was admitted after an episode of acute shortness of breath, palpitations, and diaphoresis. Initial evaluation revealed elevated troponins and BNP, leading to a diagnosis of acute pulmonary edema likely due to undetected atrial flutter. She underwent emergent dialysis with symptom improvement. Cardiac catheterization showed no significant coronary artery disease but elevated left ventricular filling pressures. A cavo-isthmic ablation was performed for atrial flutter, after which she developed rate-controlled atrial fibrillation. Anticoagulation with warfarin was initiated due to stroke risk. She was treated for a mild urinary tract infection with ciprofloxacin. Medications were adjusted, including increasing lisinopril and discontinuing lanthanum. She remained stable, with no further arrhythmias or symptoms, and was discharged home with services.
